beats.text: The whole worm was one small packet.
beats.note: The paper calls it a simple, fast scanner of 376 bytes. With headers it became a single 404 byte UDP packet.

beats.context: The entire worm, aimed at port 1434 of Microsoft SQL Server and MSDE 2000.

beats.note: Slammer began infecting hosts slightly before 05:30 UTC, according to Moore and colleagues. InfoWorld gives roughly 05:30 GMT.
It infected more than 90 per cent of vulnerable hosts within 10 minutes, and at least 75,000 hosts in total.

beats.text: The hole was known before the worm.
beats.note: The paper says David Litchfield discovered the weakness in July 2002, and Microsoft released a patch before it was publicly disclosed.
The paper says it had no malicious payload but caused harm by overloading networks. Growth slowed once bandwidth ran out.
The paper lists cancelled airline flights, interference with elections and ATM failures, including Bellevue 911 data entry terminals and part of the Bank of America ATM network.

beats.text: No malicious payload, and it still overloaded networks.
